android-interaction|Gestures.summary: The drag gestures of a Plenix app on Android: a long press (or a press on a drag handle) lifts an item, which follows the finger and lands in a list, on a target or anywhere on a board, with Material’s motion and haptics kept and the Plenix look around them: the lifted row on the raised surface, the insertion line and the target’s dashed outline in the focus ring’s color, a refusing target in the danger color with words. Every drag has a way without dragging (a Move menu, Move up and Move down, TalkBack custom actions). The other gestures (swipe, fling, pinch, pull to refresh) are the gesture foundation’s, on the same tokens. Material’s default is a list with no reorder affordance and Compose’s plain drag modifiers; Plenix adds the handle, the states and the alternatives.

variants.name: Sortable list
variants.material: LazyColumn with a drag handle (Modifier.draggable on the handle) and animateItem
variants.compose: PlenixSortableList(items, onMove) with a PlenixDragHandle per row and animateItem() on each row
variants.views: ItemTouchHelper with a SimpleCallback for up and down moves, started from the handle

variants.name: Item onto a target
variants.compose: Modifier.dragAndDropSource { … } on the item, Modifier.dragAndDropTarget(shouldStartDragAndDrop, target) on the folder
variants.views: View.startDragAndDrop and an OnDragListener on the target
variants.use: Filing an asset into a folder, a card into a column.

variants.name: Drop target
variants.material: A target with DragAndDropTarget.onEntered and onExited
variants.compose: onEntered shows the outline; a mime type it does not take shows the refusal and its words
variants.views: ACTION_DRAG_ENTERED and ACTION_DRAG_EXITED switch the target’s background
variants.use: Folders, columns and collections that take some kinds of item.

variants.name: Reposition
variants.compose: Modifier.offset { offset } from detectDragGestures, snapped to the grid on onDragEnd, with semantics customActions for TalkBack
variants.views: an OnTouchListener moving translationX and translationY, snapped on ACTION_UP
variants.use: Notes on a board, layers on a canvas.

anatomy.name: Drag handle
anatomy.about: The grip at the row’s start, at least the touch target; a long press on the row also lifts it.

anatomy.name: Lifted item
anatomy.about: The item under the finger on the raised surface, slightly transparent, above its neighbors.

anatomy.name: Insertion line
anatomy.about: A line in the focus ring’s color where the item lands in a list.

anatomy.name: Drop target
anatomy.about: A dashed outline in the focus ring’s color and the hover fill while an item it takes is over it; the danger color and words when it refuses.

anatomy.name: Move menu
anatomy.about: Move up, Move down, Move to … in the row’s menu and as TalkBack custom actions.

attributes.value: At least the touch target (PlenixPlatform.controlTargetMin, 48 dp)
The dragged opacity while it follows the finger (PlenixOpacity.opacityHigh)
The focus ring’s color, the medium border width
attributes.material: None: the list moves its rows
attributes.views: an ItemDecoration drawing a line of PlenixBorder.borderWidthMedium in PlenixColors.focusRingColor

attributes.value: A dashed outline in the focus ring’s color
attributes.material: None: the app draws its target
attributes.views: a GradientDrawable with setStroke(px(PlenixBorder.borderWidthMedium), argb(PlenixColors.focusRingColor), px(PlenixSpace.spaceInlineXs), px(PlenixSpace.spaceInlineXs))

attributes.value: The hover fill while an item it takes is over it (PlenixColors.stateHover)
The outline in the danger color (PlenixColors.feedbackDangerSolid) and words that say why
attributes.compose: the outline in PlenixColors.feedbackDangerSolid.current() and a Text that says what it takes
attributes.views: the stroke in argb(PlenixColors.feedbackDangerSolid) and a TextView

attributes.value: Move up, Move down, Move to … as menu items and TalkBack custom actions
attributes.compose: Modifier.semantics { customActions = listOf(CustomAccessibilityAction("Move up") { moveUp(); true }) }

states.compose: dragging = true from the handle’s drag start
shouldStartDragAndDrop false for the type, the refusal shown

compose: override fun onEntered(event: DragAndDropEvent) { over = true }
override fun onExited(event: DragAndDropEvent) { over = false }
override fun onDrop(event: DragAndDropEvent): Boolean { over = false; onDrop(event.toAndroidDragEvent().clipData); return true }
